headline: Malcolm Spellman Talks The Drop Spinoff
post:
Bringing back a beloved television universe takes patience and heart. According to The Hollywood Reporter, showrunner Malcolm Spellman spent over two years developing the tone for the new series before it finally clicked. The upcoming drama focuses on the rise of West Coast hip-hop during the nineteen-nineties, following familiar survivors while introducing fresh faces to the screen.

Fans hoping for a parade of familiar faces might need to adjust their expectations. The creator revealed he is "not gonna chase cameos", preferring to let familiar individuals emerge naturally when the story truly calls for it. Rather than forcing old connections, the production team focused on building an authentic world centered around community, music, and complex family dynamics.

What are you hoping to see next in the series?

original_title: Malcolm Spellman on How ‘Snowfall’ Spinoff ‘The Drop’ Connects With the Original Series and Why He’s “Not Gonna Chase Cameos”

headline: Jeff Ament looks back at Pearl Jam history
post:
Pearl Jam bassist Jeff Ament recently opened up about the band's journey and his brand-new photography book, "Since Forever", according to Rolling Stone. 📸

Before capturing iconic moments of his bandmates, Ament actually had to sell his own camera to move to Seattle in 1983. Years later, working on the movie "Singles" changed everything when the art department told him to charge a new camera to the film. That pivotal moment sparked a treasure trove of unseen historical snapshots.

While looking back through decades of memories with his brother and collaborator Barry Ament, the musician reflected on creative stress, early days, and the band's evolving journey. 🎸

What is your favorite Pearl Jam album?

#PearlJam #JeffAment #RockHistory
original_title: Jeff Ament on Pearl Jam’s Future — and Why His Band Actually Enjoyed the Nineties
